questions.prompt: Underline the final sound in fat, father, orange.
steps: Final sounds are spoken units; orange ends with /dʒ/ written ge, and father varies with accent.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.
questions.answer: fat: t; father: er (the vowel /ə/ in non-rhotic speech; r in rhotic speech); orange: ge (/dʒ/).

summaries.Oral reading: Read aloud in the printed order. Pronounce words clearly and pause at punctuation. Teachers assess accuracy and fluency; the printed text is the oral response.
summaries.Final sounds: Distinguish speech sounds from written letters. Blend consonants, recognise digraphs and compare pronunciations when identifying rhymes or homophones.
summaries.True or false: Use sentence meaning, subject agreement and time clues to choose the word or verb form. Apply the specific rule explained for each task and note ambiguous choices.
summaries.Comprehension: Find evidence in the passage or poem before answering. Distinguish explicit statements, reasonable inferences and model interpretations.
summaries.Source-limited items: The required script, picture or other information is missing. Use the stated limitation and obtain the original material before expecting a unique answer.
